topic: Quadratic-query reconstruction certificates for nonlinear latent hierarchies. On the unchanged Prashant--Ng--Zhang--Huang ICLR 2025 scalar layered-DAG class with two pure children per latent, equal measured-descendant path lengths, differentiability, conditional sufficiency, and generalized rank faithfulness, construct deterministic RankPeel using only essential-supremum ranks of observed conditional-mean Jacobians. Prove exact parentless detection, <=1 pairwise recovery of every pure block, the representative neutrality iff Pa(c) subset P, recursive full-adjacency recovery up to within-layer permutation, at most p^2+p oracle calls, O(p^3) bookkeeping, and an oracle-relative replayable certificate. Use query-specific private-path lower bounds and restricted pure-surrogate separator upper bounds; do not assume a blanket rank=minimum-separator identity, faithfulness inheritance after latent contraction, an extra saturated-rank condition, or practical CelebA consistency. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: disjoint private-path and restricted surrogate-separation arguments derive the exact rank k versus k+1 parent test at every level; 4,408 exact multilevel rational rank checks, a 36-vertex/39-edge reconstruction in 362 calls, and 192 representative-choice cases passed, while isolated blocks, parentless vertices, proportional unfaithful twins, discarded mixed descendants, correlated parents, and misleading blanket separator identities were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: independently validate the anchor's conditional separator-to-Jacobian-rank upper bound under its exact Conditions 1--3. EARLY KILL TEST: enumerate the specified 676 three-level DAGs with two extra mixed measured children and verify every proposed surrogate cut by exact d-separation; any legal counterexample stops the proof. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/eid_nonlinear_hierarchy_rankpeel_certificate.strongest_form.md

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether every latent d-separator Z used by RankPeel for observed blocks X and Y implies ess sup_x rank(D_x E[Y|X=x]) <= |Z| under the anchor's Conditions 1–3 exactly as stated, or exhibit a legal counterexample.

source_refs.claim: Theorem 1 equates conditional-mean Jacobian rank with minimum latent-separator cardinality by factoring the conditional mean through a sufficient map and applying a chain rule.
source_refs.author: Parjanya Prashant, Ignavier Ng, Kun Zhang, Biwei Huang

source_refs.claim: For linear Gaussian graphical models, low covariance-submatrix rank has an exact graphical characterization proved through trek factorizations and determinant path-polynomial arguments.
source_refs.author: Seth Sullivant, Kelli Talaska, Jan Draisma

open_problems.why_unsolved: The anchor's upper-bound argument writes the observed conditional mean as h(g(x)), but its stated conditions separately guarantee differentiability of g and of the final observed conditional mean without plainly guaranteeing differentiability of h or justifying differentiation through the defining conditional-distribution integral. Linear trek-separation results obtain analogous upper bounds from finite algebraic factorizations and therefore do not settle this nonlinear analytic step. Generalized faithfulness cannot repair an upper bound that has not first been graphically and analytically entailed.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a theorem deriving the essential-supremum Jacobian-rank upper bound for every explicitly specified RankPeel surrogate cut from Conditions 1–3, with the factorization and differentiation steps justified, or a smooth scalar SEM satisfying those conditions and the asserted d-separation while violating the bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from latent-hierarchy nonidentifiability to an observable Jacobian-rank criterion while isolating the one-way implication actually needed by reconstruction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonlinear latent hierarchies evade covariance-rank methods -> conditional-mean Jacobians expose observable low-dimensional structure -> the separator-to-rank implication must hold under the stated model conditions

method_exemplars.technique: Separate the always-valid separator-induced matrix factorization from the generic lower bound based on vertex-disjoint trek systems and determinant expansions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired resolution likewise needs to distinguish query-specific graphical upper bounds from noncancellation or faithfulness arguments used for lower bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent rank inequalities using trailing singular-value functionals and calibrate their nonregular null distribution with a second-order bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once queried Jacobians are estimated, the proved upper bounds become composite rank restrictions with the same irregular lower-rank boundary geometry.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the Prashant–Ng–Zhang–Huang population rank oracle be compiled into a deterministic algorithm that recovers every pure block and all latent adjacencies using at most p^2+p observed-block queries and emits a replayable certificate for every decision?

source_refs.claim: Theorem 3 gives recursive identifiability, but its proof identifies pure blocks and mixed-child parent sets by checking families of subsets rather than providing a bounded observed-query protocol.
source_refs.author: Parjanya Prashant, Ignavier Ng, Kun Zhang, Biwei Huang

source_refs.claim: In a different latent-variable model, the authors give polynomial-time leaf-to-root and root-to-leaf recovery with an error signal when their assumptions fail.
source_refs.author: Xiuchuan Li, Tongliang Liu

source_refs.claim: Covariance-rank tests reconstruct linear latent hierarchies asymptotically, but under IL2H restrictions and only up to the paper's minimal-graph and skeleton operators.
source_refs.author: Biwei Huang, Charles Jia Han Low, Feng Xie, Clark Glymour, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The anchor's constructive proof uses exhaustive subset predicates and invokes a latent-level oracle after deleting a layer; it supplies neither an observed-rank query bound nor a transcript locally witnessing each recovered block and edge. Related polynomial-time and rank-based algorithms operate in different latent models or recover weaker graph objects. The first proof step that must change is pure-block discovery: the all-subsets criterion must be replaced by pairwise private-path lower bounds and restricted pure-surrogate separator upper bounds without invoking a blanket rank-equals-minimum-separator identity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A deterministic RankPeel oracle algorithm with a theorem proving exact pure-block and full-adjacency recovery up to within-layer permutation, at most p^2+p essential-supremum Jacobian-rank calls, O(p^3) bookkeeping, and a transcript whose recorded queries and comparisons certify every output decision.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its exact scalar layered-DAG model and identifiability-to-algorithm narrative while making oracle complexity and certification the missing constructive layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Population Jacobian ranks identify nonlinear latent structure -> the published construction searches large subset families and recurses abstractly -> a bounded deterministic protocol is needed for auditable reconstruction

method_exemplars.technique: Recover latent structure sequentially across layers and couple the recovery procedure to an explicit assumption-violation signal.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its trustworthiness theorem is the nearest published analogue of a replayable structural certificate, although its observables and assumptions differ.

method_exemplars.technique: Use observed pure descendants as rank-test surrogates, refine initial clusters, and recover higher layers recursively.
method_exemplars.why_closest: RankPeel must likewise represent latent vertices by observed descendants while preventing spurious clusters during recursive peeling.

method_exemplars.technique: Test composite rank inequalities through trailing singular-value functionals with bootstrap control at lower-rank boundary points.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is a natural inference module for replacing exact certificate entries with statistically calibrated rank decisions.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the weakest replacement for Condition 3(ii), p(z|x)=p(z|g(x)) with dim(g)=|z|, under which the restricted conditional-mean Jacobian queries needed by RankPeel still identify the unchanged scalar layered DAG.

source_refs.claim: The conclusion identifies possible relaxation of Condition 3 as future work and reports empirical recovery in settings where it may fail.
source_refs.author: Parjanya Prashant, Ignavier Ng, Kun Zhang, Biwei Huang

source_refs.claim: Nonlinear latent hierarchies are identified by a different route requiring latent variables and exogenous noise to be recoverable as differentiable invertible functions of observations.
source_refs.author: Lingjing Kong, Biwei Huang, Feng Xie, Eric P. Xing, Yuejie Chi, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Condition 3(ii) is the anchor's mechanism for forcing an observed conditional mean through a |Z|-dimensional bottleneck, but it is stronger than conditional independence alone and is neither shown necessary nor characterized. The alternative invertible-recovery literature imposes a different and stronger recovery condition. What remains missing is an operator-level condition that yields the restricted upper and lower ranks used by reconstruction without asserting a global minimum-separator identity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient or sharply sufficient condition on the relevant conditional-expectation operators under which every RankPeel query has its prescribed rank, together with a nonidentifiability or rank-failure construction immediately outside that condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its conclusion explicitly exposes Condition 3 as a restriction to relax, and its proof identifies where the condition enters the rank argument.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional sufficiency creates a low-dimensional observable bottleneck -> the stated condition appears stronger than reconstruction requires -> isolate the exact operator property needed by the restricted queries

method_exemplars.technique: Build hierarchical identification from an elementary nonlinear latent-variable identifiability criterion and an explicit layerwise construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an alternative nonlinear route to layerwise identification when the anchor's conditional-sufficiency factorization is unavailable.

method_exemplars.technique: Factor observed conditional means through low-dimensional sufficient statistics and convert that factorization into Jacobian-rank restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested characterization must preserve precisely this bottleneck mechanism on the smaller family of reconstruction queries.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish uniform approximations and feasible inference for functional transformations of nonparametric regression estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An observable version of a weaker operator condition must ultimately support uniform estimation of the resulting conditional-mean derivatives.

open_problems.open_problem: Is generalized conditional-mean-Jacobian rank faithfulness generic for the anchor's nonlinear SEM class under a well-defined parameterization, or can structural dependence among Jacobian factors produce positive-size families of unentailed rank cancellations?

source_refs.claim: Proposition 1 argues that generalized-faithfulness violations have measure zero by invoking full rank of products of continuously drawn random matrices.
source_refs.author: Parjanya Prashant, Ignavier Ng, Kun Zhang, Biwei Huang

source_refs.claim: Linear Gaussian generic rank faithfulness follows from explicit determinant path polynomials and a graph-theoretic trek-separation characterization.
source_refs.author: Seth Sullivant, Kelli Talaska, Jan Draisma

open_problems.why_unsolved: The anchor's supporting lemma concerns products of random matrices with continuously distributed entries, whereas Jacobians generated by one SEM are functionally dependent across factors, query points, and variable sets. An unrestricted differentiable-function class also lacks a canonical Lebesgue measure. Linear trek theory avoids this ambiguity because relevant minors are finite polynomials in structural coefficients and their nonvanishing can be witnessed combinatorially; a nonlinear analogue needs an explicit parameter space and genericity notion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A genericity theorem for a specified nonlinear SEM parameter space showing that every graphically nonentailed queried Jacobian minor is nonzero outside a null or meagre set, or a parametric family satisfying the baseline conditions on which an unentailed rank drop persists on an open positive-measure set.

writing_exemplar.why: Retain its generalized-faithfulness motivation while making the probability space and structural dependence of the Jacobians explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rank recovery must exclude accidental cancellations -> the anchor claims such cancellations are measure zero -> nonlinear structural Jacobians require a rigorous genericity notion and proof

method_exemplars.technique: Exhibit a nonzero determinant monomial from a disjoint path system and infer generic nonvanishing because the determinant polynomial is not identically zero.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result must likewise distinguish graph-forced rank drops from parameter cancellations, but for conditional-mean Jacobian minors.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cancellation-free expansions to certify nonzero Gaussian graphical-model subdeterminants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A cancellation-free or sign-controlled nonlinear representation would directly address structurally dependent Jacobian factors.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct rank tests valid at singular and lower-rank null points instead of assuming a regular full-rank boundary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Nearly unfaithful models generate the weak-singular-value regimes in which ordinary rank asymptotics fail.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a finite-sample, replayable RankPeel procedure whose adaptively selected essential-supremum conditional-mean-Jacobian rank decisions jointly recover the latent graph with an explicit high-probability guarantee.

source_refs.claim: The population theory treats Jacobian rank as an exact graphical oracle, while its implementation does not estimate and test the theorem's adaptive rank-query transcript.
source_refs.author: Parjanya Prashant, Ignavier Ng, Kun Zhang, Biwei Huang

source_refs.claim: Rank <= r is an irregular composite null, so procedures calibrated only at rank exactly r can over-reject when the true rank is smaller.
source_refs.author: Qihui Chen, Zheng Fang

source_refs.claim: Uniform partitioning-based nonparametric inference supplies strong approximations and feasible procedures for functional transformations of regression estimators.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Yulong Shigida

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the growing-depth two-point family by an alphabet-budgeted packing and pair it with finite-order filtering.
Derive a dependent growing-window process approximation for PHIW centered at the target, retaining selection.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature separates uniform nonparametric derivative inference from nonregular matrix-rank testing, but does not compose them for a supremum-over-conditioning-values oracle whose later queries depend on earlier answers. The prior proposal independently exposes the same two boundaries in a latent model: finite latent complexity does not ensure stable recovery without rank separation, and validity after data-dependent history selection is distinct from a fixed-statistic limit theorem. RankPeel therefore needs simultaneous, selection-stable confidence sets over its adaptive query tree, including near-ties between the k and k+1 singular-value regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A concrete conditional-Jacobian estimator and adaptive rank-testing rule with simultaneous confidence statements, an explicit sample-complexity bound in p, smoothness, conditioning density, and singular-value margins, and a theorem giving uniform familywise coverage and exact-graph recovery for the complete replay certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Frame inference as the missing bridge between its population Jacobian criterion and data-level certified latent-graph recovery.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Population Jacobian ranks identify latent structure -> samples provide noisy nonparametric conditional means -> adaptive peeling compounds rank uncertainty -> simultaneous control is required for graph-wide certification

method_exemplars.technique: Derive uniform Bahadur representations and strong approximations for partitioning-based nonparametric estimators and their functional transformations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Essential-supremum Jacobian queries require uniform rather than pointwise control of derivatives of conditional-mean estimators.

method_exemplars.technique: Use sums of trailing squared singular values and a second-order bootstrap for composite rank nulls.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each oracle decision is an irregular matrix-rank test, including cases where the true rank lies below the tested boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate local rank-test decisions through latent-cluster construction and recursive edge refinement.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest causal-graph template for converting a collection of noisy rank decisions into global latent-structure recovery.

literature_map:
1. Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang (ICLR 2025; arXiv:2411.19556) introduce conditional-mean Jacobian ranks for nonlinear latent hierarchies under two-pure-child, equal-depth, generalized-faithfulness, and conditional-sufficiency conditions.
2. Their separator/rank theorem relies on induced-map differentiability and generic-rank steps that mark the principal proof boundary for restricted RankPeel cuts.
3. Their recursive identifiability construction checks subset families and supplies no quadratic observed-query bound or replayable certificate.
4. Kong et al. (NeurIPS 2023; arXiv:2306.07916) identify nonlinear latent hierarchies through an alternative invertible latent/noise recovery route.
5. Huang et al. (NeurIPS 2022; arXiv:2210.01798) recover linear latent hierarchies through covariance ranks and recursive observed surrogates, but return a weaker graph object under IL2H restrictions.
6. Dong et al. (ICLR 2024; arXiv:2312.11001) allow hidden variables throughout linear partially observed networks, including measured parents, without a nonlinear Jacobian analogue.
7. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma (Annals of Statistics 2010; arXiv:0812.1938) prove trek-separation rank results by separating graph-forced factorizations from generic determinant noncancellation.
8. Draisma, Sullivant, and Talaska (2013; arXiv:1210.0390) provide cancellation-free subdeterminant expansions relevant to a rigorous faithfulness argument.
9. Silva et al. (JMLR 2006) and Kummerfeld–Ramsey (KDD 2016; DOI:10.1145/2939672.2939838) recover pure measurement structure through linear tetrad-style footprints.
10. Li and Liu (ICLR 2025; OpenReview:BZYIEw4mcY) provide polynomial-time, assumption-aware recovery in another latent model and the closest framing for trustworthy discovery.
11. Li, Wang, and Liu (ICLR 2025; OpenReview:fGhr39bqZa) replace pure children with homologous surrogates, while Lee and Gu (2025; arXiv:2505.18410) use double-triangular conditions for binary-latent nonparametric models.
12. Chen and Fang (Quantitative Economics 2019; arXiv:1812.02337) establish the nonregularity of composite matrix-rank inference and give a second-order bootstrap.
13. Cattaneo, Feng, and Shigida (Annals of Statistics 2026; arXiv:2409.05715) supply uniform inference for nonparametric regression functionals, but not its composition with adaptive graph-reconstruction queries.
14. The closest opportunities are restricted separator-bound validation, quadratic-query certified reconstruction, rigorous generalized-rank-faithfulness genericity, weaker operator conditions, and simultaneous finite-sample rank inference.
